foodForest.title: Moringa
lines: 1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: Leaves and green pods; keep their records separate.

First crop reference: 6–12 months. The 6–12-month reference concerns the first leaf harvest after planting. Flowers and pods are normally produced during the second year of growth in the same North West guide. Leaf readiness does not establish pod production or picking months. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Pod development, not a young green-pod picking calendar: This botanical description discusses pods that become brown at maturity. The separate harvesting section requires young, tender, green pods for food and supplies no calendar for that stage. March–April is retained as pod-development phenology, not a confirmed young-pod picking season or leaf calendar.
Choose a sunny, well-drained growing position, protect establishment and plan pruning for leaf harvest.
Buying advice: Use correctly identified local planting material. No locally validated named cultivar shortlist is sourced; this plan does not claim nitrogen fixation or medicinal effects.
Expected picking season: no fixed regional months sourced. Record planting and picking dates locally.

foodForest.title: Avocado
lines: 1 existing; 1 proposed. Products: fruit.

First crop reference: 2–3 years. Bruyns Hill, Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2; irrigated Hass on clonal Duke 7 rootstock, 7 x 7 m (200 trees/ha), planted 1982–1984. The paper reports Hass starting in its second season and Fuerte in its third. The two-to-three-year reference describes those trial cultivars, not every avocado or nursery starting age. Actual timing depends on variety and site care.

Established production reference: 6–8 years. In this irrigated, intensively managed Natal Midlands trial, Hass reached about 20 t/ha at age 6 and orchards approached maximum sustainable average yield by age 8. This is a trial-specific bearing reference; there is no national plateau or automatically interpolated age-yield curve.

Production reference: 100–112.5 kg/plant. Same-trial arithmetic at the initial 200 trees/ha: 20,000 kg/ha / 200 = 100 kg/tree at age 6; sustainable average 22,500 kg/ha / 200 = 112.5 kg/tree. At age 3, 10,000 kg/ha / 200 = 50 kg/tree equivalent. These are average-equivalent reference values for the named Hass/Duke 7 orchard conditions, not measured individual-tree yields or default production for a different density, cultivar, climate or management. Intermediate ages are not inferred.

Hass age benchmarks — irrigated Natal Midlands trial: Hass on Duke 7, initially 200 trees/ha at Bruyns Hill (Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2), with intensive irrigation and nutrition. Age 3: 10,000 kg/ha; age 6: 20,000 kg/ha; sustainable average about 22,500 kg/ha. Same-study density permits equivalents of 50 kg/tree at age 3 and 100 kg/tree at age 6; there is no reference for every intermediate age. These orchard benchmarks are conditional on good resources, comparable climate and timely orchard management, including Phytophthora control and thinning; do not auto-fill farm quantities.
Keep roots well drained; water matters during flowering.
Buying advice: KZN sequence: earlier Fuerte (May–Nov), middle Hass (Aug–Dec), later Ryan (Nov–Feb). These seasons overlap. Buy labelled grafted trees; confirm rootstock and pollination partners.
Pollination: partly self fertile. Check the chosen cultivar's requirements with the nursery.
Assumed variety: Hass. South Africa - warm subtropical regions (Hass cultivar). Planning reference when established; confirm local picking dates. No food quantity or first-year crop promised.

Foraging alone may not supply enough nutrients for eggs.

climateNotes.text: Growing water is limited. Check drinking water separately; garden water does not confirm a safe poultry supply.
You reported wet ground. Check that chicken housing drains and bedding stays dry.
You reported frost. Check winter shelter and chick warmth with a local adviser.

options.name: Potchefstroom Koekoek
options.detail: An egg-and-meat option. It outperformed the other indigenous breeds for eggs in a managed ARC trial; those results do not predict this farm.

options.name: Venda
options.detail: An ARC-conserved indigenous option for eggs and meat; check local stock and care needs.

options.name: Ovambo
options.detail: An ARC-conserved indigenous option for eggs and meat; check local stock and care needs.

options.name: Naked Neck
options.detail: An indigenous option described across diverse South African climates; confirm suitability with local advice.

options.name: Commercial layers — egg system
options.detail: Consider only after checking reliable feed, drinking water, housing, health care and managed lighting. Breed and supplier still need local confirmation.

options.name: Commercial broilers — meat system
options.detail: Needs dependable balanced feed, water, suitable housing and management. Confirm chick supply and a meat outlet before choosing.

poultryGuidance.localCheck: These are options to discuss, not a final breed recommendation. Confirm healthy stock, supplier availability, ventilation, chick warmth and a health plan locally. Record actual production months separately; this guide promises no output or dates.
